label: Where will your software run?
help: This decides whether the system can be split into separate services on servers. A website that works on phones runs on your server; a phone app people download counts as an app.

options.label: Not sure
options.description: Every style stays in the running.

options.label: On our server, used in a web browser
options.description: Websites, web apps, admin portals and APIs. People on phones open it in their browser.

options.label: On our server, plus an app people download
options.description: A mobile or desktop app (e.g. from an app store) that talks to our server.

options.label: Only on the user's own device, with no server of ours
options.description: A program that works on its own, e.g. a text editor, a photo editor or an offline game.

label: Do all parts of the system need the same qualities?
help: Qualities are things like speed, uptime, handling many users and security. Most systems are "Yes", even with several screens or user groups.

options.label: Not sure
options.description: The ranking won't lean either way.

options.label: Yes, roughly the same everywhere
options.description: E.g. a booking or records system where every part needs similar uptime and security.

options.label: No, some parts need very different things
options.description: E.g. a public shop that must survive huge traffic spikes next to a back office that mainly needs strict security.
